page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.large is an entry-level virtual server instance within the ecs.e family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs, which are mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core). The CPU allocation is shared, meaning compute resources are shared with other tenants. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned for low-intensity workloads. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1284.39, while the multi-core score reached 1722.27, placing it in the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 94.5 GB/sec, but large block uncached read and write speeds drop to 2.01 GB/sec and 1.99 GB/sec respectively. Geekbench metrics reflect similar constraints, with a single-core score of 724.0 and a multi-core score of 774.0. Database operations and web serving capabilities are also modest, with Redis SET operations handling 1.35 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 0.26 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and entry-level performance metrics, the ecs.e-c1m4.large offers a highly cost-efficient profile for non-critical, low-demand environments. The primary tradeoff is the potential for resource contention due to the shared CPU model, alongside limited memory bandwidth and lack of local storage. This instance is best suited for lightweight applications, basic development and testing environments, simple text processing, and low-traffic static web serving where high-performance compute is not required.
